Question: How should one deal with this at a restaurant, ordering a steak dinner with baked potato and actually being served instant potatoes instead, and the manager saying they had run out of baked potatoes?
Answer: I spent the better part of my youth working in food service and making a living on tips and made a really good living too, I would be really upset at my manager if they substituted instant potatoes for a baked potato without telling me so I could then tell my customer. A good restaurant and a good server will inform the customer that they ran out of something so then the customer can decide what they would like as a substitution. While many restaurants do have a clause on the menu in fine print that states substitutions may be made or something to that effect, that clause really should only be used as a shield from abusive customers. It should never be a restaurants policy. As a food server I would not be happy and I would really expect the manager to comp the meal (give for free) or at the least give a free dessert or something to the customer if they served them a plate of food they changed without asking first. If they did not do that minor bit of an apology I would start looking for another place to work. Since restaurants do not pay much and I had to rely on tips I need to work in a place that lets me earn as much as I can, not tie my hands. How I would deal with it as a customer who was told by the manager they changed something without asking me first would be to politely say that I wished that they would have asked me first and then if I really did not want instant potatoes and ask for something else. If they did not accommodate me I’d still pay for the meal but I’d let them know that I most likely would not return. Honestly even if they just honored my request without apology I’d still probably not come back. Now if the manager apologized and offered me a token like a free dessert I would surely come back. If the food was good I’d tell others as well. Things go wrong and things do run out. Sometimes the kitchen makes a mistake so if my complaint is acknowledged I know it is a well run establishment.

Question: Have you ever said anything to your boss that got you fired?
Answer: Have you ever said anything to your boss that got your fired? Yes, but I had already quit at that point. Let me explain. I was working at a 4 star hotel in Downtown Los Angeles as a bartender in their main lounge. It was a pretty ritzy club that played live jazz and had a fantastic buffet. I had worked there for about two years when we got a new manager and he decided to turn the place into a sports bar. He took the bar from a place selling Cognac and Martini’s to 5 dollar pitchers of beer. Gone was the live music and it was replaced with a juke box. Gone was the buffet and it was replaced with pretzels and buffalo wings. My nightly tips dropped severely. Probably lost a couple hundred dollars a week. Combine that with the fact this guy was a real pain-in-the-ass to work for and well, I knew it was time for another job. Next to the hotel was a high-end restaurant and the managers would often come into the bar for drinks after their shift. They learned of my displeasure and quickly offered me a job at the restaurant tending bar. I had quite a following of patrons that were not happy with the new management either and they would surely follow me next door. It was a pretty easy decision. So I have my two weeks notice. I could have quit and started the new job right away but I’ve always felt giving notice was the right thing to do and you might as well not burn any bridges on the way out if you can avoid it. Here’s where it went terribly wrong. From that point on, the manager started treating me like crap and rode my ass constantly. The night I was fired was a busy Friday night. We were open til 1AM and at about Midnight I would start cleaning things up and get ready for closing. At that point the manger looks at me and slaps his forehead “Oops man I forgot it’s bug night (bug night was the pest control spraying they would do every other month) which meant I’d have take every item out from behind the bar and put it way and cover it. This was a huge bar I was working. Ok it wasn’t this exact bar, but it was like two of these. This was going to be about 2 hours of work on top of the normal closing routine. It was well after midnight and the manager was sitting at the bar devouring a plate of nachos. I started grabbing glasses and bottles and piling them up and just kept watching these guy hoofing cheese covered corn chips in his maw and the anger was building. Me: “So your not going to help at all?” Him: “Nope” Me” Really? It’s after midnight, this is going to take hours.” Him: “Yeah I forgot, sorry. You’ll have to manage it somehow.” I couldn’t hold my tongue anymore. Thanks for reading this far - Here’s what I said that got me fired I’m a pretty calm guy, I mean like I’m famous for my calm (well among my friends and associates anyways) and I blew up. Me: “I tell you what, you get up off your ass and help me with this or you’re going to have to do it yourself” Him: He wipes his mouth with a napkin and stands up. “So you’re refusing to do this? You are actually refusing to do your job?” Me: Yes, I guess I am. I need help with this or your doing this yourself. He then walks over to the phone and calls security. They show up and ask what’s going on. He says I’m refusing to work and I need to have my register counted out and be escorted off the premises. My anger had left me at that point and I was just relieved to get out of there. That was the only job I’ve had where I both quit and been fired.

Question: How do I convert an appearance pattern to vector in Illustrator whilst maintaining transparency?
Answer: For simplicity I’m assuming you have a black & white pattern and you want the white part transparent though this will work regardless of the colors as long as you have solid shapes in the raster image you want to convert to vectors. After conversion I’d expect you to have black shapes and white shapes in that graphic, the white shapes will be filled and will not be transparent if you use something like the auto trace feature of Illustrator. There may be a setting to use that I’m not familiar with but what I’d do in this situation is click on a white shape after it is turned to a vector and select all with the same color fill option. That will select all the white parts and you should be able to delete them thus having a “transparent” background. If the black and white shapes and connected and you can’t delete the white without the black going away then here is a hack I discovered. Select all of the same fill as I mentioned above. All of the white shapes will highlight (even though they may be connected to the black) Select “hide” for the white parts you selected. Select “show hidden” the white will come back but this time only the white parts you want to delete will be really selected. Now you can delete at will. As an alternative you could just make the white fill in the shapes transparent but I think best practice would be to remove unneeded shapes in the graphic. Some images are more complex than others so results will vary. For the best chances of converting your pattern from raster to vector you want the sharpest image with the most solid colors and the most contrast between shapes you can start with. I often photoshop the image and blow the contrast to the max. Hope that is clear. If not ask and I’ll try to clarify. Good luck.

Question: I have a doc in CMYK mode in Illustrator. When printing on flat paper, the color is perfect. When on glossy, it is a completely different color. How do I adjust settings in Illustrator to work with my printer and the glossy paper?
Answer: I know your frustration but as far as I know for CMYK printing there is no function in Illustrator to preview various paper types. It would not make sense for this function because Gloss coated stocks vary from vendor to vendor and each and change the final output of your artwork. So many times I had customers upset about their finished piece when they printed a beautiful color image onto an uncoated stock. These papers will absorb some of the ink and therefore change the color, sometimes drastically, much to a customers surprise. I did my best to catch this and advise the customer when I could but you can’t anticipate what everyone’s expectations are. There is no real substitution for a proof printed on the paper type you will output on if you have any concerns about the final color.

Question: Given the choice, would you store all of your food / leftovers in glass instead of plastic? Do you limit heating food to non-plastic containers or is this too much effort?
Answer: Glass or Plastic? Plastic and Glass food storage containers both have their uses. I like plastic better overall for storage as it is lighter and more durable (they don’t break when you drop them…usually!) I avoid plastic when storing acidic foods like tomato sauce. Mostly it is because the plastic gets stained but I also can’t help but think there is some transfer of materials going on and extra plastic in my sauce is not something I’d want. Glass containers do have a much longer lifetime. In fact I usually only throw out a glass container because it’s plastic lid has degraded beyond use, not because the glass has anything wrong with it. Replacing the lid costs about as much as a new container too - what’s up with that? (Rhetorical question) For reheating food, I do try to avoid plastic because I’m told the chemicals will leech into your food. I do try to put in some effort for this but, if it don’t work out I don’t sweat it very much. How can I worry about a little plastic leeching into my food when I live in a world surrounded by chemicals? Living among things like electricity, fume belching engines, household cleansers, etc, leads me to conclude to not over worry about one container. I don’t think the extra plastic in my container is going to tip the balance in what I am exposed to. Still, I avoid reheating in plastic when I can.

Question: What recipes or hacks do you have to reduce food waste at home?
Answer: I’m probably a bad person to ask how to reduce food waste because I probably waste a ton of food. I cook more than I can eat and usually have to toss some away because I get lazy about packing and freezing stuff for later. My biggest tip would be to not cook more than you can eat! That said, I do have some ways I do like to use up food that may be getting a bit old or is leftover from other meals instead of throwing it out. Soups: You can toss almost anything in a pot of water and season it enough to make a decent soup. If I have any leftover veggies that are getting a bit too old to eat raw, some leftover cooked meats (Ham and Pork bones are great), I toss them into a pot with some chicken broth or water and bouillon if I don’t have any broth around. You can even toss in a can of beans or some pasta if you want to bulk it up a bit. Toss in a little salt & pepper and maybe a bay leaf and slow cook it for a couple hours and you can have a delicious soup. Fritattas: This is like a quiche but without the pastry crust. It’s just eggs and whatever you have laying around, then you bake it in a skillet in the oven. Your base is eggs, a splash of milk or cream or even butter, then just toss in whatever you have laying around. Meats, cheese, veggies, whatever. Another good leftover clearer. Smoothies: Have some fruit thats too ripe to eat? I hate mushy fruit, there’s nothing unhealthy about it and it’s really sweet and flavorful but I can’t get past the mushy texture. So I toss that ripe fruit in the blender with some yogurt or almond milk or ice, or any other liquid I have around and blend it up into a yummy smoothie. Salads: Have some leftover chicken, turkey or ham? Chop it up into small bits, mix in some celery, onion, carrot, or red peppers minced up small if you have it, add few spoonfuls of mayo and you got your self a meal!. I can eat this in a sandwich, or over some lettuce. Even can just eat it in a bowl with some crackers. It’s a good way to get rid of leftovers without tossing it away. I hope this inspires you to use up some of the food you might be tossing away.

Question: What will happen to the economy when there are only billionaires and poor people and the poor can't afford to buy the products made by companies owned by the billionaires?

If there were only billionaires and poor people, that would indicate that all markets have collapsed. At this point the billionaires have consolidated all power to themselves and we’d be practically back in a feudal system. There’d be no point in making more money selling things to the masses because the point of money (for the rich) is power and if everyone was poor that’d mean the billionaire's already had all the power. I suspect the world would evolve into something like this. Lazarus is a comic that portrays a dystopian future where corporations have taken over the world. They have consolidated themselves the the point that a few families own and operate these corporations and have divided the world up among themselves. The social order of the world is simple. You are either one of the family (one of the billionaires), you are a citizen (the people deemed productive: Doctors, security, craftsmen, etc.) or you are Waste (everyone else). The world population is like 95% waste. Each family group handles their waste differently. Some give basic charities. Some treat them with indifference leaving them to fend for themselves as long as they don’t interfere with family business. Some are treated no better than slaves, infected with diseases that only the family has the cure for. To me this is exactly what would happen if there were only Billionaires and poor. We’d be back to feudal times. Kings and Serfs.

Question: Why do PNG files sometimes have "black" backgrounds even though they are transparent?
Answer: Why do PNG files sometimes have “black” backgrounds even though they are transparent? Your question needs more context. What are you trying to accomplish that the black backgrounds are appearing? I’m going to assume you mean printing. This is by far the most common action where I can get odd backgrounds and other printing errors involving a transparent background Depending on what program you are using and what print settings you are using, transparent objects do not always play nice and you can get boxes, missing pieces, strange colors and background shades appearing around your transparent object. The majority of the time I find it is a spot color that is causing the issue. Spot colors and transparency do not play nice with each other. No matter the cause, the best method of fixing it is flattening transparency. Each program does it in a different way so you need to see if you have any options to flatten the transparency. Flattening transparency will take all the objects on your page and flatten them into one single image thus eliminating your software from having to interpret what is going on. There’s a more technical way to describe it but I’m going for simplicity in my explanation. You might ask why we don’t just flatten everything to avoid problems in the first place. There is a good reason. Flattening transparency can cause problems as well. You have to pay careful attention to your fonts, images and any special effects such as drop shadows in case something changes in them when you flatten transparency. Also your flattened file will also be much, much larger than your original. Basically it turns your artwork into one large image. This could cause a printer to crash if you don’t have the processing power to print very large file sizes. If you are going to a commercial printer it will take them a lot longer to process and print a large file so this might be a consideration too if you are in a super rush. Without knowing more about your specific situation this is the best guess I can offer as to what is causing problems.

Question: Does light blue here demonstrated using CMYK on the website I linked to in the comments look purple to anyone else or am I colorblind?
Answer: It looks light blue to me on my monitor. The problem with viewing colors on a screen is everyone’s monitor and lighting conditions is different, this is aside from the RGB/CMYK issues. You can actually get a decent representation of CMYK on your monitor if it is calibrated properly to the device you are printing from. This is why when printing CMYK colors, you never, ever want to proof your colors on a monitor if color is any sort of concern for you. If that swatch looks purple to you on screen I suggest adjusting your monitor. Since you know that it is supposed to be light blue, adjust til you see light blue and you have a very “rough” color calibration for your output.
